short.AMD: Most of these articles are opinion pieces, but they point to a few reported facts. AMD posted Q3 revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45%, with data center sales nearly doubling, and it completed an $8.2 billion acquisition of World Labs. The stock fell after earnings and again after new Commerce Department export limits on Southeast Asia, where Singapore was 12.4% of 2025 revenue. Opinions on whether it is a good buy differ.
short.NVDA: Nvidia reported Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103%, and raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75%, but its shares still fell after CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid personal allegations and CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. Investors are also weighing export curbs, regulatory scrutiny and $118 billion in financial guarantees. All the articles are opinion pieces, and they disagree on whether the leadership change is a risk or an opportunity.
short.META: These articles are mostly opinion pieces, with no single new company event. One factual thread is that Meta borrowed about $25 billion this month, lifting debt to roughly $109 billion while spending heavily on AI (2026 capex of $135-145B). Commentators disagree: some stress strong ad growth and a modest valuation, others warn of shrinking margins and Reality Labs losses.
